articles.headline: OFAC Designates Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations in Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Action
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new designations targeting Guatemalan drug trafficking organizations. This action, taken on November 13, 2026, falls under OFAC's Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism programs.

Specifically, OFAC added 'LOS LORENZANAS' (also known as the LORENZANA DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION, THE LORENZANA CLAN, and THE LORENZANA FAMILY) to its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. This entity is identified as a Transnational Terrorist Group and Criminal Organization.

Additionally, the 'LOS MENDOZA DRUG TRAFFICKING ORGANIZATION,' operating in Guatemala, Honduras, and Belize, was also designated. This organization is linked to the SINALOA CARTEL and is targeted under authorities related to illicit drugs.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran-Related SDN Listing for Volta Shipping Services LLC
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an update to an Iran-related entry on its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List on November 9, 2026. This action is part of ongoing efforts to counter Iranian sanctions evasion.

The update specifically concerns Volta Shipping Services LLC, a UAE-based company linked to Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani. OFAC changed its listed alias from Volta Shipping Services FZCO to Volta Container Line FZCO.
Volta Shipping Services LLC remains designated under Executive Order 13902, which targets key sectors of the Iranian economy, and continues to be subject to secondary sanctions risk.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Canada-Based Money Services Businesses Tied to Iran's Digital Asset Sector
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated eight Canada-based money services businesses on November 6, 2026, for their alleged involvement in Iran's digital asset sector. This action is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' and aims to disrupt international financial channels used by Iran to evade sanctions.

These businesses are accused of facilitating transactions involving Iran, including converting Iranian currency into digital assets and conducting transactions with sanctioned Iranian exchanges and digital asset addresses linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

The designations were coordinated with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), Canada's financial intelligence unit (FINTRAC), and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), and were taken under Executive Order 13902.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: U.S. Expands Cuba Sanctions to Key Economic Sectors and Designates Related Entities
body: The United States issued new Cuba-related sanctions on November 5, 2026, targeting a crude oil shipping network, state-owned entities, and China-based suppliers of Cuba's military forces. Concurrently, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) published a determination extending Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine.
This action allows the U.S. government to block the property of non-U.S. persons determined to operate in these newly designated sectors or to have materially assisted the Government of Cuba.

Among the entities designated were China National Electronic Import and Export Company (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation, for their alleged work with Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A., a Cuban arms procurement entity.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Network, Issues Alert on Shadow Fleet, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, targeting four individuals and nine entities linked to an India-based network supporting Iran's shadow fleet. This network, allegedly led by Suniel Kumar Sharma and Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, is accused of providing false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels transporting Iranian petroleum.
Concurrently, OFAC issued an alert warning against the Iranian shadow fleet's use of false flags for sanctions evasion.

In a separate action, OFAC issued Amended Venezuela-related General License (GL) 5AA, which authorizes transactions related to, financing for, and other dealings in the Petróleos de Venezuela, S.A. 2020 8.5 percent bond, effective December 18, 2026. This new GL replaces and supersedes GL 5Z.

body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026. This amendment modifies existing authorizations related to transactions involving Iran.

Further details regarding the scope and implications of this amended General License are available on the Treasury Department's website. Parties involved in Iran-related transactions are advised to review the updated guidance to ensure compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo-Related Entities
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter illicit activities and human rights abuses. The North Korea designations aim to disrupt revenue generation for the regime, while the DRC designations target those allegedly supporting armed groups in the region.
Further details on the specific individuals and entities designated, as well as the authorities under which these actions were taken, are available on OFAC's website.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for $1.53 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026, for $1,529,685. The settlement resolves nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The violations stemmed from exports from the United States to JSC Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian missile manufacturer, between September 2018 and March 2022. MMZA was majority-owned by the sanctioned state-owned defense company JSC Concern Almaz Antey and was considered blocked under OFAC's 50 Percent Rule throughout the relevant period.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were voluntarily self-disclosed but egregious. The compliance failures were attributed to insufficient due diligence by Extreme Networks following its Russian subsidiary's purchase of customer accounts and contracts, which included MMZA as an end user.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs Regarding Blocking and Rejecting Transactions and Filing Reports
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, concerning blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments aim to provide updated guidance and clarification for financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.

Entities subject to OFAC's jurisdiction are encouraged to review the updated FAQs to ensure their internal procedures align with the latest requirements for reporting and handling blocked or rejected transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026, as part of its ongoing efforts to counter illicit Iranian activities.
In the same action, OFAC also announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions against these countries.
Additionally, OFAC issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions, providing updated guidance for various transactions.

articles.headline: EU Imposes Sweeping Sanctions on Russian Banks, Shadow Fleet, and Disinformation Networks
body: The European Union has imposed a new package of sanctions on Russia, targeting 12 individuals and 101 entities, including nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions. This move aims to further restrict Russia's ability to finance its war against Ukraine and respond to indiscriminate attacks on civilian infrastructure.

The sanctions also target Russia's online retail sector, specifically the sole shareholder of Wildberries and an individual controlling a majority stake in Ozon, two of Russia's largest e-commerce platforms, which the EU states serve as supply networks for the Russian military.

Additionally, the EU sanctioned 30 individuals and two entities over Russian foreign information manipulation, interference, and malicious cyber activities targeting EU states, institutions, and partners. Among these are the Moscow-based Social Design Agency (SDA) and the pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16).

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
